editorial:
Imagine being the smartest and funniest guy in the room, but you are too shy to date the girl of your dreams because of a giant nose. That is exactly where you find Cyrano, a brave soldier and poet in old France who is deeply in love with the beautiful Roxane. The problem is that Roxane likes Christian, a handsome soldier who has no idea how to talk to women. In a wild twist, Cyrano decides to help Christian by writing all the romantic letters and speeches for him. It is a sweet and funny setup that makes you root for the underdog while wondering if the truth will ever come out.

You will love the energy of the sword fights and the way the actors bring these big emotions to life. While some of the dialogue feels a bit old-fashioned, the heart of the story is timeless. If you enjoy stories about secret crushes and sacrifice, you have to see this.
endingExplained: Years later, Cyrano visits Roxane one last time. She finally realizes that the beautiful letters she loved all those years ago were actually written by Cyrano, not Christian. It is a heartbreaking moment because they spent their whole lives missing out on each other. Cyrano is badly injured and dies shortly after, but he leaves with his honor and spirit intact, knowing that Roxane finally knows the truth about his love.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic romance and stories about secret love.
